materials.name: facade_glass
materials.note: Glass is a dielectric. Near-mirror roughness so the sun reads as a tight glint and the sky reflects; anything above ~0.2 and glazing stops looking like glass at this scale.

materials.name: facade_mullion
materials.note: 1960s curtain walls: anodized aluminum. Not mirror-smooth -- the anodizing scatters, and on low-poly geometry a tighter lobe strobes as facets cross the highlight.

materials.name: building_wall
materials.note: Brick, stucco and concrete facade mass. Near-fully rough: masonry has no specular lobe worth the name at this scale, and lowering it makes a whole block read as wet plastic. Base colour tints the era palette rather than replacing it.

materials.name: building_roof
materials.note: Tar, slate and parapet caps. Slightly smoother than the walls so roofs catch a little sky and read as a separate plane from above -- the main thing that stops a massing model looking like one extruded blob.
